questions.q: Let a rectangle $A B C D$ of sides 2 and 4 be inscribed in another rectangle $P Q R S$ such that the vertices of the rectangle $A B C D$ lie on the sides of the rectangle $P Q R S$. Let $a$ and $b$ be the sides of the rectangle $P Q R S$ when its area is maximum. Then $(a+b)^2$ is equal to :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Area }=(4 \cos \theta+2 \sin \theta)(2 \cos \theta+4 \sin \theta) \\ & =8 \cos ^2 \theta+16 \sin \theta \cos \theta+4 \sin \theta \cos \theta+8 \sin ^2 \theta \\ & =8+20 \sin \theta \cos \theta \\ & =8+10 \sin 2 \theta \\ & \text { Max Area }=8+10=18(\sin 2 \theta=1) \theta=45^{\circ} \\ & (a+b)^2=(4 \cos \theta+2 \sin \theta+2 \cos \theta+4 \sin \theta)^2 \\ & =(6 \cos \theta+6 \sin \theta)^2 \\ & =36(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)^2 \\ & =36(\sqrt{2})^2\end{aligned}$ $=72$

questions.q: Let the set of all positive values of $\lambda$, for which the point of local minimum of the function $\left(1+x\left(\lambda^2-x^2\right)\right)$ satisfies $\frac{x^2+x+2}{x^2+5 x+6} < 0$, be $(\alpha, \beta)$. Then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is equal to _________
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{x^2+x+2}{x^2+5 x+6} < 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{(x+2)(x+3)} < 0\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & x \in(-3,-2) \ldots \ldots \ldots . .(1) \\ & f(x)=1+x\left(\lambda^2-x^2\right) \end{aligned}$
Finding local minima $f^{\prime}(x)=\left(\lambda^2-x^2\right)+(-2 x) \cdot x$ Put $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=0$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \lambda^2=3 x^2 \\ & \Rightarrow x= \pm \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}} \end{aligned}$ We want local min $\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{-\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}$ from (1) $x \in(-3,-2)$ $\begin{aligned} & -3 < \frac{-\lambda}{\sqrt{3}} < -2 \\ & 3 \sqrt{3}>\lambda>2 \sqrt{3} \\ & \alpha=2 \sqrt{3}, \beta=3 \sqrt{3} \\ & \alpha^2+\beta^2=12+27=39\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $5f\left(x\right) + 4f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = {x}^{2} - 2, ∀ x \ne 0$ and $y = 9{x}^{2}f\left(x\right),$ then $y$ is strictly increasing in:
questions.solution:
Given: $5f\left(x\right) + 4f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = {x}^{2} - 2 . . . \left(i\right)$

Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac{1}{x}$.

$⇒ 5f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + 4f\left(x\right) = {\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)}^{2} - 2 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Using, $\left(i\right) \times 5 - \left(ii\right) \times 4$

$⇒ 25f\left(x\right) + 20f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) - 16f\left(x\right) - 20f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = 5{x}^{2} - 10 - \dfrac{4}{{x}^{2}} + 8$

$⇒ 9f\left(x\right) = 5{x}^{2} - \dfrac{4}{{x}^{2}} - 2$

Now, $y = 9f\left(x\right) \times {x}^{2}$

$⇒ y = \left(5{x}^{2} - 2 - \dfrac{4}{{x}^{2}}\right) \times {x}^{2}$

$⇒ y = 5{x}^{4} - 2{x}^{2} - 4$

$⇒ {y}^{'} = 20{x}^{3} - 4x$

$⇒ {y}^{'} = 4x\left(5{x}^{2} - 1\right)$

For function to be increasing ${y}^{'} > 0$

$⇒ x \in \left(- \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{5}}, 0\right) ∪ \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{5}}, \infty\right)$

questions.q: The area enclosed by the curves $xy + 4y = 16$ and $x + y = 6$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given: $xy + 4y = 16, x + y = 6$

$⇒ \left(6 - x\right)\left(x + 4\right) = 16$

$⇒ 6x + 24 - {x}^{2} - 4x - 16 = 0$

$⇒ - {x}^{2} + 2x + 8 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 2x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 4\right)\left(x + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 4, - 2$

So, the required area is given by,

$A = \mathop{∫}_{- 2}^{4}\left(\left(6 - x\right) - \left(\dfrac{16}{x + 4}\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ A = {\left[6x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - 16log\left|x + 4\right|\right]}_{- 2}^{4}$

$⇒ A = \left(24 - 8 - 16log\left|8\right|\right) - \left(- 12 - 2 - 16log2\right)$

$⇒ A = 16 - 16log\left|8\right| + 14 + 16log2$

$⇒ A = 30 - 32ln2$

questions.q: Three points $O\left(0, 0\right), P\left(a, {a}^{2}\right), Q\left(- b, {b}^{2}\right), a > 0, b > 0,$ are on the parabola $y = {x}^{2}$. Let ${S}_{1}$ be the area of the region bounded by the line $PQ$ and the parabola, and ${S}_{2}$ be the area of the triangle $OPQ$. If the minimum value of $\dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}}$ is $\dfrac{m}{n}, gcd\left(m, n\right) = 1,$ then $m + n$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Plotting the diagram of the given data we get,

Area of $△ OPQ$ is given by,

${S}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 1 \\ a & {a}^{2} & 1 \\ - b & {b}^{2} & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ {S}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(a{b}^{2} + {a}^{2}b\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, equation of line $PQ: y - {a}^{2} = \dfrac{{a}^{2} - {b}^{2}}{a + b}\left(x - a\right)$

$⇒ y - {a}^{2} = \left(a - b\right)x - \left(a - b\right)a$

$⇒ y = \left(a - b\right)x + ab . . . \left(ii\right)$

Area bounded by the line $PQ$ and the parabola is given by,

${S}_{1} = \mathop{∫}_{- b}^{a}\left(\left(a - b\right)x + ab - {x}^{2}\right)dx$

$⇒ {S}_{1} = {\left[\left(a - b\right)\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \left(ab\right)x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right]}_{- b}^{a}$

$⇒ {S}_{1} = \dfrac{{\left(a - b\right)}^{2}\left(a + b\right)}{2} + ab\left(a + b\right) - \dfrac{\left({a}^{3} + {b}^{3}\right)}{3} . . . \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{\left(a - b\right)}^{2}}{2} + ab - \dfrac{\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2} - ab\right)}{3}}{\dfrac{ab}{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{3{\left(a - b\right)}^{2} + 6ab - 2\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2} - ab\right)}{3ab}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{3\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2} - 2ab\right) + 6ab - 2\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2} - ab\right)}{3ab}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{3{a}^{2} + 3{b}^{2} - 6ab + 6ab - 2{a}^{2} - 2{b}^{2} + 2ab}{3ab}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + 2ab}{3ab}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{a}{b} + \dfrac{b}{a} + 2\right]$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}}\right)}_{min} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[1 + 1 + 2\right]$ $\left\{\text{as}\dfrac{a}{b} + \dfrac{b}{a} \ge 2\right\}$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{{S}_{1}}{{S}_{2}}\right)}_{min} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ m + n = 7$

questions.solution:
Given,

And $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{\lim_{r \to x}\left\{\dfrac{2{r}^{2}\left[( f ( r ) {)}^{2} - f ( x ) f ( r )\right]}{{r}^{2} - {x}^{2}} - {r}^{3}e\dfrac{f ( r )}{r}\right\}}$

$⇒ {f}^{2} ( x ) = \lim_{r \to x}\left(\dfrac{2{r}^{2}\left({f}^{2} ( r ) - f ( x ) f ( r )\right)}{{r}^{2} - {x}^{2}} - {r}^{3}e\dfrac{f ( r )}{r}\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{2} ( x ) = \lim_{r \to x}\left(\dfrac{2{r}^{2}f ( r )}{r + x}\dfrac{( f ( r ) - f ( x ) )}{r - x} - {r}^{3}e\dfrac{f ( r )}{r}\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{2} ( x ) = \dfrac{2{x}^{2}f ( x )}{x + x}\left(\lim_{r \to x}\dfrac{( f ( r ) - f ( x ) )}{r - x}\right) - {x}^{3}e\dfrac{f ( x )}{x}$

$⇒ {f}^{2} ( x ) = \dfrac{2{x}^{2}f ( x )}{2x}{f}^{'} ( x ) - {x}^{3}e\dfrac{f ( x )}{x}$

Now, taking $f\left(x\right) = y$ we get,

$⇒ {y}^{2} = xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} - {x}^{3}e\dfrac{y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{y}e\dfrac{y}{x}$

Now, let $y = vx ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$⇒ v = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} - \dfrac{x}{v}{e}^{v}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{{e}^{v}}{v}$

$⇒ {e}^{- v}vdv = dx$

Integrating both side

${e}^{v} ( x + c ) + 1 + v = 0$

Now using $f ( 1 ) = 1 ⇒ x = 1, y = 1$ we get,

$⇒ c = - 1 - \dfrac{2}{e}$

Hence, ${e}^{v}\left(- 1 - \dfrac{2}{e} + x\right) + 1 + v = 0$

$⇒ e\dfrac{y}{x}\left(- 1 - \dfrac{2}{e} + x\right) + 1 + \dfrac{y}{x} = 0$

Now taking, $x = a \text{ and } y = 0$ we get,

${e}^{0}\left(- 1 - \dfrac{2}{e} + a\right) + 1 + 0 = 0$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{2}{e}$

$⇒ ae = 2$

$⇒ c = 0$

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{a - bcos2x}{{x}^{2}}; x < 0 \\ {x}^{2} + cx + 2; 0 \le x \le 1 \\ 2x + 1; x > 1\end{array}\right$

If $f$ is continuous everywhere in $R$ and $m$ is the number of points where $f$ is NOT differential then $m + a + b + c$ equals:
questions.explanation:
At $x = 1, f\left(x\right)$ is continuous,

$⇒ f\left({1}^{-}\right) = f\left(1\right) = f\left({1}^{+}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = 3 + c . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ f\left({1}^{+}\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}2\left(1 + h\right) + 1$

$⇒ f\left({1}^{+}\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}3 + 2h = 3 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Using $\left(i\right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$,

$⇒ c = 0$

At $x = 0, f\left(x\right)$ is continuous,

$⇒ f\left({0}^{-}\right) = f\left(0\right) = f\left({0}^{+}\right) . . . \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ f\left(0\right) = f\left({0}^{+}\right) = 2 . . . \left(iv\right)$

So, $f\left({0}^{-}\right)$ has to be equal to $2$.

$⇒ \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{a - bcos\left(2h\right)}{{h}^{2}}$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{a - b\left\{1 - \dfrac{4{h}^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{16{h}^{4}}{4 !} + . ..\right\}}{{h}^{2}}$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{a - b + b\left\{2{h}^{2} - \dfrac{2}{3}{h}^{4} . ..\right\}}{{h}^{2}}$

For limit to exist $a - b = 0$ and limit is $2b$$. . . \left(v\right)$

Using, $\left(iii\right), \left(iv\right)\text{and}\left(v\right)$

$⇒ a = b = 1$

Checking differentiability at $x = 0$.

$⇒ LHD: \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{1 - cos2h}{{h}^{2}} - 2}{- h}$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{4{h}^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{16{h}^{4}}{4 !} - . ..\right) - 2{h}^{2}}{- {h}^{3}} = 0$

$⇒ RHD: \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{{\left(0 + h\right)}^{2} + 2 - 2}{h} = 0$

Function is differentiable at every point in its domain

$∴ m = 0$

$⇒ m + a + b + c = 0 + 1 + 1 + 0$

$⇒ m + a + b + c = 2$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{1 - sin2x}dx = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2} + \gamma\sqrt{3}$, where $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are rational numbers, then $3\alpha + 4\beta - \gamma$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{1 - sin2x}dx = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2} + \gamma\sqrt{3}$

Now, let $I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{1 - sin2x}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} | sinx - cosx | dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} ( cosx - sinx ) dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} ( sinx - cosx ) dx$

$⇒ I = - 1 + 2\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3}$

Now, comparing with 

$I = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2} + \gamma\sqrt{3}$

We get, $\alpha = - 1, \beta = 2, \gamma = - 1$

Hence, $3\alpha + 4\beta - \gamma = - 3 + 8 + 1 = 6$

questions.q: The value $9{∫}_{0}^{9}\left[\sqrt{\dfrac{10x}{x + 1}}\right]dx$, where $t$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$, is _____.
questions.solution:
Let,

$I = {∫}_{0}^{9}\left[\sqrt{\dfrac{10x}{x + 1}}dx\right]$

The square of integers are $0, 1, 4, 9, . . .$

$⇒ 0 = \dfrac{10x}{x + 1} ⇒ x = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ 1 = \dfrac{10x}{x + 1} ⇒ x + 1 = 10x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{9} . . . \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 4 = \dfrac{10x}{x + 1} ⇒ 4x + 4 = 10x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ 9 = \dfrac{10x}{x + 1} ⇒ 9x + 9 = 10x$

$⇒ x = 9 . . . \left(iv\right)$

Now, from the above equations using the law ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{a}^{c}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_{c}^{d}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_{d}^{b}f\left(x\right) d x$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{9}}\left(0\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{9}}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}\left(1\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{2}{3}}^{9}\left(2\right)dx$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{9} + 2\left(9 - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{155}{9}$

$⇒ 9I = 155$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}cosxdx}{\left(1 + {e}^{sinx}\right)\left(1 + \sin^{4}x\right)} = \alpha\pi + \beta{\log}_{e}\left(3 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)$, where $\alpha, \beta$ are integers, then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}$ equals __________
questions.solution:
Given: $I = \mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}cosx}{\left(1 + {e}^{sinx}\right)\left(1 + \sin^{4}x\right)}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Applying ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right) d x$ rule we get,

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}cosx\left({e}^{sinx}\right)}{\left(1 + {e}^{sinx}\right)\left(1 + \sin^{4}x\right)}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding $\left(i\right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 2I = \mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}cosx}{1 + \sin^{4}x}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}cosx}{1 + \sin^{4}x}dx$

Putting, $sinx = t$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{1 + {t}^{4}}dx$

$⇒ I = 4\sqrt{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}}{{t}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}} - \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}}{{t}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = 4\sqrt{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}}{{\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2} + 2} - \dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)}{{\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2} - 2}\right)dt$

Let $t - \dfrac{1}{t} = z$ and $t + \dfrac{1}{t} = k$

$⇒ I = 4\sqrt{2}\left[\mathop{∫}_{- \infty}^{0}\dfrac{dz}{{z}^{2} + 2} - \mathop{∫}_{\infty}^{2}\dfrac{dk}{{k}^{2} - 2}\right]$

$⇒ I = 4\sqrt{2}{\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{z}{\sqrt{2}}\right]}_{- \infty}^{0} - {\left[\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}ln\left(\dfrac{k - \sqrt{2}}{k + \sqrt{2}}\right)\right]}_{\infty}^{2}$

$⇒ I = 4\sqrt{2}\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\left[ln\dfrac{2 - \sqrt{2}}{2 + \sqrt{2}}\right]\right]$

$⇒ I = 2\pi + 2log\left(3 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)$

Comparing this value with $\left[\alpha\pi + \beta{\log}_{e}\left(3 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)\right]$

$⇒ \alpha = 2$ and $\beta = 2$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} = 8$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2{x}^{3} - 3{x}^{2} - x + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2{x}^{3} - 3{x}^{2} - x + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

Using $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right)dx = 0$ when$f\left(2a - x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

Now, finding $f\left(1 - x\right)$ we get,

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2{\left(1 - x\right)}^{3} - 3{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2} - \left(1 - x\right) + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2\left(1 - {x}^{3} - 3x + 3{x}^{2}\right) - 3{\left(1 + {x}^{2} - 2x\right)}^{2} - \left(1 - x\right) + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2 - 2{x}^{3} - 6x + 6{x}^{2} - 3 - 3{x}^{2} + 6x - 1 + x + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(- 2{x}^{3} + 3{x}^{2} + x - 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = - I$

$⇒ f\left(1 - x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

$∴ I = 0$

questions.q: Let $f: \left(0, \infty\right) \to R$ and $F\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}tf\left(t\right)dt$. If $F\left({x}^{2}\right) = {x}^{4} + {x}^{5},$ then $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}f\left({r}^{2}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given: 

$F\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}t ⋅ f\left(t\right)dt$

Now, applying Newton Leibnitz Theorem we get,

${F}^{'}\left(x\right) = x ⋅ f\left(x\right)$

 And $F\left({x}^{2}\right) = {x}^{4} + {x}^{5}$

Let ${x}^{2} = t$

$⇒ F\left(t\right) = {t}^{2} + t\dfrac{5}{2}$

$⇒ {F}^{'}\left(t\right) = 2t + \dfrac{5}{2}t\dfrac{3}{2}$ $\left\{\text{as}{F}^{'}\left(x\right) = x ⋅ f\left(x\right)\right\}$

$⇒ t ⋅ f\left(t\right) = 2t + \dfrac{5}{2}t\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ f\left(t\right) = 2 + \dfrac{5}{2}t\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}f\left({r}^{2}\right) = \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}2 + \dfrac{5}{2}r$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}f\left({r}^{2}\right) = 24 + \dfrac{5}{2}\left[\dfrac{12\left(13\right)}{2}\right]$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}f\left({r}^{2}\right) = 219$

Let, $sinx = t$

$cosxdx = dt$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1 + {t}^{2}}{1 + {t}^{4}}dt$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}}{{t}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}}dt$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)$

questions.solution:
Equation of $CE$ is given by,

$⇒ \left(y - 1\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{3 - 2}{2 - 1}}\left(x - 3\right)$

$⇒ \left(y - 1\right) = - ( x - 3 )$

$⇒ x + y = 4 . . . \left(i\right)$

Similarly, equation of $AD$ is given by,

$⇒ \left(y - 2\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{3 - 1}{2 - 3}}\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(y - 2\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ 2y - 4 = x - 1$

$⇒ x - 2y + 3 = 0$

Using $\left(i\right)$

$⇒ 4 - y - 2y + 3 = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{7}{3}$

$⇒ x = 4 - \dfrac{7}{3}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{5}{3}$

So, Orthocentre is $H ≡ \left(a, b\right) = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right)$.

Orthocentre lies on the line $x + y = 4$

So, $a + b = 4$

Now, ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b}xsin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx . . . ( 1 )$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b} ( a + b - x ) sin ( \left(a + b - x\right) ( 4 - \left(a + b - x\right) ) ) dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b} ( 4 - x ) sin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx . . . ( 2 )$

Using, $( 1 ) + ( 2 )$

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b}4sin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx$

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = 4{I}_{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{I}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{36{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = 72$

Then the value of $9\left(f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9} + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right\right)\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given: $g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{{x}^{2}}t\dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{- t}dt$

Let, $t = {y}^{2}$

$⇒ dt = 2ydy$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}2{y}^{2}{e}^{- {y}^{2}}dy$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}{t}^{2}{e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$

Also, $f\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}\left(t - {t}^{2}\right){e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$y

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}t{e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$

Let, ${t}^{2} = p$

$⇒ 2tdt = dp$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{e}^{- p}dp$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = 1 - {e}^{- {x}^{2}}$

$⇒ 9f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) = 9\left(1 - {e}^{- log9}\right)$

$⇒ 9f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) = 9\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{9}\right)$

$⇒ 9f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) = 8$

questions.solution:
Given: 

$y = f\left(x\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = {f}^{'}\left(x\right)$

${\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}_{\left(1, f\left(1\right)\right)} = {f}^{'}\left(1\right) = tan\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} . . . \left(i\right)$

${\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}_{\left(3, f\left(3\right)\right)} = {f}^{'}\left(3\right) = tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(3\right) = 1 . . . \left(ii\right)$

It is given that, $27{∫}_{1}^{3}\left({\left({f}^{'}\left(t\right)\right)}^{2} + 1\right){f}^{"}\left(t\right)dt = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{3}$

Let, $I = {∫}_{1}^{3}\left({\left({f}^{'} ( t )\right)}^{2} + 1\right){f}^{"}\left(t\right)dt$

Putting, ${f}^{'} ( t ) = z ⇒ {f}^{"}\left(t\right)dt = dz$

$z = {f}^{'} ( 3 ) = 1$

$z = {f}^{'}\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}\left({z}^{2} + 1\right)dz$

$⇒ I = {\left(\dfrac{{z}^{3}}{3} + z\right)}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}$

$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{1}{3} + 1\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{3}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{10}{9\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta\sqrt{3} = 36 - 10\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \alpha = 36, \beta = - 10$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = 36 - 10$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = 26$

questions.q: $\left|\dfrac{120}{{\pi}^{3}}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{x}^{2}sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx\right|$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{x}^{2}sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

Now using the property ${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(2a - x\right) d x$ we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}\left({x}^{2} - {\left(\pi - x\right)}^{2}\right) d x$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}\left(2\pi x - {\pi}^{2}\right) d x$

$⇒ I = 2\pi\mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{x \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} - {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

Now, solving ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{x \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx . . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding both equations we get,

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx$

Now, putting the value in $I$ we get,

$⇒ I = 2\pi \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{x \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx - {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{1 - 2\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}sin2x}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{2}2x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sin2x}{2 - \sin^{2}2x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sin2x}{1 + \cos^{2}2x} d x$

Now, let $cos2x = t ⇒ - 2sin2xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{1}^{- 1}\dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 + {t}^{2}} d t$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4}{∫}_{- 1}^{1}\dfrac{1}{1 + {t}^{2}} d t$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{3}}{8}$

Hence, $\dfrac{120}{{\pi}^{3}}\left|{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{x}^{2}sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x\right| = \dfrac{120}{{\pi}^{3}} \times \dfrac{{\pi}^{3}}{8} = 15$

Given: $secxdy + \left\{2\left(1 - x\right)tanx + x\left(2 - x\right)\right\}dx = 0$

$⇒ secxdy = \left\{2\left(x - 1\right)tanx + \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right)\right\}dx$

questions.solution:
Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sqrt{\sin^{3}x\cos^{3}xsin ( x - \theta )}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sqrt{\sin^{3}x\cos^{3}x ( sinxcos\theta - cosxsin\theta )}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sqrt{\sin^{3}x\cos^{4}x ( tanxcos\theta - sin\theta )}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x}{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x\cos^{2}x\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sin^{2}xcos\dfrac{3}{2}x\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{1}{\sin^{2}x\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}x}{\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{{cosec}^{2}x}{\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

So, $I = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} . . . . \left\{let\right\}$

For ${I}_{1}$, let $tanxcos\theta - sin\theta = {t}^{2}$

$⇒ cos\theta \times {sec}^{2}xdx = 2tdt$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = \dfrac{2tdt}{cos\theta}$

For ${I}_{2}$, let $cos\theta - cotxsin\theta = {z}^{2}$

$⇒ {cosec}^{2}x \times sin\thetadx = 2zdz$

$⇒ {cosec}^{2}xdx = \dfrac{2zdz}{sin\theta}$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{2tdt}{cos\theta \times t} + ∫ \dfrac{2zdz}{sin\theta \times z}$

$⇒ I = 2\left[\left(sec\theta\right) ∫ \left(1\right)dt + cosec\theta ∫ \left(1\right)dz\right]$

$⇒ I = 2sec\theta\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta} + 2 cosec \theta\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}$

$⇒ A \times B = 4sec\thetacosec\theta$

$⇒ A \times B = \dfrac{2}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{sin\thetacos\theta}$

$⇒ A \times B = 8 cosec 2\theta$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a differentiable function in the interval $(0, \infty)$ such that $f(1)=1$ and $\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1$ for each $x>0$. Then $2 f(2)+3 f(3)$ is equal to _______
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1 \\
& \lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{2 t . f(x)-x^2 f^{\prime}(x)}{1}=1 \\
& 2 x \cdot f(x)-x 2 f^{\prime}(x)=1 \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{2}{x} \cdot y=\frac{-1}{x^2} \\
& \text { I.f. }=e^{\int-\frac{2}{x} d x}=\frac{1}{x^2} \\
& \therefore \frac{y}{x^2}=\int-\frac{1}{x^4} d x+C \\
& \frac{y}{x^2}=\frac{1}{3 x^3}+C
\end{aligned}$
Put $f(1)=1$
$\begin{aligned} & C=\frac{2}{3} \\ & y=\frac{1}{3 x}+\frac{2 x^2}{3} \\ & y=\frac{2 x^3+1}{3 x} \\ & f(2)=\frac{17}{6} \\ & f(3)=\frac{55}{9} \\ & 2 f(2)+3 f(3)=\frac{17}{3}+\frac{55}{3}=\frac{72}{3}=24\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}x - 1, x\text{is even}, \\ 2x, x\text{is odd},\end{array}\rightx \in N$. If for some $a \in N, f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 21$, then $\lim_{x \to {a}^{-}}\left\{\dfrac{{\left|x\right|}^{3}}{a} - \left[\dfrac{x}{a}\right]\right\},$ where $\left[t\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$, is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}x - 1; x\text{is even} \\ 2x: x\text{is odd}\end{array}\right$

And $f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 21$

Case-I: If $a$ is even

$⇒ f\left(a\right) = a - 1 = \text{Odd}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(a\right)\right) = 2\left(a - 1\right) = \text{Even}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 2a - 3 = 21$

$⇒ a = 12$

Case-II: If $a$ is odd

$⇒ f\left(a\right) = 2a = \text{Even}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(a\right)\right) = 2a - 1 = \text{Odd}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 4a - 2 = 21$ (Not possible)

Hence, $a = 12$

Now,$\lim_{x \to {12}^{-}}\left(\dfrac{{\left|x\right|}^{3}}{12} - \left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]\right) = \lim_{x \to {12}^{-}}\dfrac{{\left|x\right|}^{3}}{12} - \lim_{x \to {12}^{-}}\left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {12}^{-}}\left(\dfrac{{\left|x\right|}^{3}}{12} - \left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]\right) = 144 - 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {12}^{-}}\left(\dfrac{{\left|x\right|}^{3}}{12} - \left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]\right) = 144$

Then $\mathrm{k}^2$ is equal to ________

$\begin{aligned} & \sum_{\mathrm{r}=1}^{\infty} \frac{\mathrm{n}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{n}^4+\mathrm{r}^4}}-\frac{2 \mathrm{nr}^2}{\left(\mathrm{n}^2+\mathrm{r}^2\right) \sqrt{\mathrm{n}^4+\mathrm{r}^4}} \\ & \sum_{\mathrm{r}=1}^{\infty} \frac{\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}}{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{n}}\right)^4}}-\frac{2\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{n}}\right)^2}{\left(1+\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{n}}\right)^2\right) \sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{n}}\right)^4}} \\ & \Rightarrow \int_0^1 \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^4}}-\frac{2 \mathrm{x}^2 \mathrm{dx}}{\left(1+\mathrm{x}^2\right) \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^4}} \\ & \Rightarrow \int_0^1 \frac{1-\mathrm{x}^2}{\left(1+\mathrm{x}^2\right) \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^4}} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \int_0^1 \frac{\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}-1}{\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right) \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}}} \mathrm{dx}\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow-\int_0^1 \frac{1-\frac{1}{x^2}}{\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right) \sqrt{\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)^2-2}} d x \\ & x+\frac{1}{x}=t \Rightarrow 1-\frac{1}{x^2} d x=d t\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow-\int_{\infty}^2 \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{t} \sqrt{\mathrm{t}^2-2}} \\ & \Rightarrow-\int_{\infty}^2 \frac{\mathrm{tdt}}{\mathrm{t}^2 \sqrt{\mathrm{t}^2-2}} \\ & \text { take } \mathrm{t}^2-2=\alpha^2 \\ & \mathrm{tdt}=\alpha \mathrm{d} \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow-\int_{\infty}^{\sqrt{2}} \frac{\alpha \mathrm{d} \alpha}{\left(\alpha^2+2\right) \alpha} \\ & \Rightarrow-\int_{\infty}^{\sqrt{2}} \frac{\mathrm{d} \alpha}{\alpha^2+2}\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \left.\Rightarrow \frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1} \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{2}}\right]_{\infty}^{\sqrt{2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\left\{\tan ^{-1} 1\right\}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1} \infty \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{4 \sqrt{2}}=\frac{\pi}{\mathrm{K}} \end{aligned}$
So $\mathrm{K}=4 \sqrt{2}$ $\mathrm{K}^2=32$

questions.solution:
Given, $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{e}^{2\left|sinx\right|} - 2\left|sinx\right| - 1}{{x}^{2}}$

Now, using the expansion of ${e}^{x} = 1 + \dfrac{x}{1 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + . . . . . . . . \infty$ we get,

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{\left|2sinx\right|}{1 !} + \dfrac{{\left|2sinx\right|}^{2}}{2 !} + . . . . . \infty\right) - \left|2sinx\right| - 1}{{x}^{2}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{2\sin^{2}x + \dfrac{{\left|2sinx\right|}^{3}}{3 !} . . . . . \infty}{{x}^{2}}$

$= 2\left\{\text{as}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{{x}^{2}} = 1\text{and other terms will become zero}\right\}$

(II) $R$ is transitive Then which one of the following is true?

All $\left(\left(\mathrm{x}_1 \mathrm{y}_1\right),\left(\mathrm{x}_1, \mathrm{y}_1\right)\right)$ are in $\mathrm{R}$ where
$\mathrm{x}_1, \mathrm{y}_1 \in \mathrm{N} \therefore \mathrm{R}$ is reflexive
$((1,1),(2,3)) \in \mathrm{R} \text { but }((2,3),(1,1)) \notin \mathrm{R}$
$\therefore \mathrm{R}$ is not symmetric
$((2,4),(3,3)) \in \mathrm{R}$ and $((3,3),(1,3)) \in \mathrm{R}$ but $((2,4)$,
$(1,3)) \notin \mathrm{R}$
$\therefore \mathrm{R}$ is not transitive
